title: Unfiltered Olive Oil Sounds Like A Good Idea. In Most Cases, It's Not.
excerpt: Unfiltered olive oil looks more natural, but the residual water and sediment accelerate oxidation — destroying the polyphenols and flavour you're paying for. Unless you're at the mill, filtered is the better buy.
seoTitle: Unfiltered Olive Oil Sounds Like A Good Idea. In Most Cases, It's Not.
seoDescription: Unfiltered olive oil degrades faster than filtered. The sediment and water that make it cloudy accelerate oxidation, destroying polyphenols and flavour.
